text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions, which means choosing clear and meaningful names for variables and functions. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. When code is well organized, it becomes much easier to maintain and update over time. Good maintainability saves time and reduces mistakes when changes are needed. In short, writing clean code helps teams work together more effectively and keeps projects healthy in the long run.
